preconditions.description: The graph has n vertices, m edges, and k special vertices, with constraints on their sizes.

preconditions.expression: len(v_special) == int(k) and all(1 <= v <= int(n) for v in v_special) and len(set(v_special)) == int(k)
preconditions.description: The k special vertices are distinct and within the valid range.

preconditions.expression: len(c) == int(n) and all(0 <= c_i <= 10**9 for c_i in c)
preconditions.description: The c array has n elements, each representing a vertex's reward, within valid bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(w) == int(m) and all(0 <= w_i <= 10**9 for w_i in w)
preconditions.description: The w array has m elements, each representing an edge's undirected cost, within valid bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == int(m) and all(1 <= x <= int(n) and 1 <= y <= int(n) and x != y for x, y in edges)
preconditions.description: The edges are valid pairs of distinct vertices within the graph.

preconditions.expression: all(x != y for x, y in edges) and all(x == y or (x, y) not in edges for x, y in edges)
preconditions.description: There is at most one edge between each pair of vertices.

postconditions.expression: len(output) == int(n) and all(isinstance(p, int) for p in output)
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n integers, one for each vertex.

postconditions.expression: all(-10**18 <= p <= 10**18 for p in output)
postconditions.description: Each output value is a valid profit (within reasonable bounds).

postconditions.expression: all(p == max_profit_for_vertex(i, n, m, k, v_special, c, w, edges) for i, p in enumerate(output, start=1))
postconditions.description: For each vertex i, the output is the maximum profit achievable when vertex i must be saturated.
